articles.title: Daryl Mitchell breaks 27-year-old New Zealand record against India, joins elite list
articles.summary: Daryl Mitchell has rewritten the record books with another milestone against India, becoming the New Zealand batter with the most ODI runs against the Men
articles.body: Daryl Mitchell has rewritten the record books with another milestone against India, becoming the New Zealand batter with the most ODI runs against the Men in Blue in a calendar year.The right-hander achieved the feat during the second ODI of the ongoing series at Wellington's Hnry Stadium on Saturday, November 7, moving past former New Zealand all-rounder Chris Cairns' long-standing record.Mitchell needed 24 runs to surpass Cairns' tally of 403 runs, accumulated across 11 ODIs in 1999. He reached the landmark by scoring his 24th run off the fifth delivery of the 19th over.The 2026 campaign has been particularly productive for Mitchell against India. He had already made 84, 131 not out and 137 during the three-match ODI series between the two sides in January. He also scored 28 in the opening match of the ongoing five-match series in Auckland on November 4.With 435 runs to his name in just five ODIs against India in 2026, Mitchell has moved to the top of New Zealand's list for the most ODI runs against India in a calendar year. Cairns now occupies the second position, followed by Kane Williamson (361) and Ross Taylor (343).Mitchell breaks Williamson's New Zealand recordMitchell's latest achievement has also seen him go past another significant milestone. His tally of 435 runs has surpassed Kane Williamson's record for the most ODI runs scored by a New Zealand batter against a single opposition in a calendar year.Dilshan holds overall record against IndiaWhile Mitchell has taken the New Zealand record, the overall benchmark for the most ODI runs against India in a calendar year remains with former Sri Lanka captain Tillakaratne Dilshan.Dilshan amassed 592 runs in 12 matches against India in 2009, a record that continues to stand. West Indies great Chris Gayle occupies second place with 558 runs from 10 matches in 2002, while former England opener Marcus Trescothick is third with 545 runs from 11 innings in the same year.Australia's Usman Khawaja is fourth with 539 runs in 2019, while West Indies legends Gordon Greenidge and Vivian Richards occupy the fifth and sixth positions with 533 and 532 runs respectively.Most ODI runs against India in a calendar yearPlayerCountryMatchesInningsRunsBest score100s50sYearTillakaratne DilshanSri Lanka1212592160212009Chris GayleWest Indies1010558140322002Marcus TrescothickEngland1111545121222002Usman KhawajaAustralia99539104232019Gordon GreenidgeWest Indies1111533115141983Vivian RichardsWest Indies1110532149211983Kumar SangakkaraSri Lanka121252790052009David BoonAustralia1313522111131986Ramnaresh SarwanWest Indies101051399*042002Geoff MarshAustralia1212512125211986Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'God did not accept it': Ex-India cricketer on Mohammed Shami's unfulfilled Test comeback
articles.summary: Bengal head coach Laxmi Ratan Shukla is disappointed that Mohammed Shami could not make a comeback to India's Test team before announcing his retirement
articles.body: Bengal head coach Laxmi Ratan Shukla is disappointed that Mohammed Shami could not make a comeback to India's Test team before announcing his retirement from the format.Shukla said he and many others wanted the senior fast bowler to return to the Indian team and end his Test career while wearing the India jersey. However, he felt that fate had other plans for the 36-year-old pacer.Shami announced his retirement from Test cricket on Friday night, bringing an end to a 13-year career in which he picked up 229 wickets in 64 matches, including six five-wicket hauls.Shami last played a Test for India in the 2023 World Test Championship final against Australia. Despite not being part of India's Test plans since then, he continued to play domestic cricket for Bengal.“Despite all of that, playing and practising for Bengal for the last two years in Ranji Trophy, Mushtaq Ali, and Vijay Hazare - I mean, you are the best, Shami.“You are outstanding. We all wanted you to have a comeback in the Test team and retire from there. But God did not accept it. Despite that, you are the best,” Shukla said in a video posted on his Instagram account.Shukla praises Shami's hard workThe former India all-rounder also praised Shami for the hard work he put in for Bengal despite having played international cricket for many years.Shukla said he had rarely seen a fast bowler work so hard for domestic cricket after achieving so much at the international level.“Outstanding Mohammed Shami. A wonderful record in Test cricket for a wonderful player and human being.“I would like to share one more thing with all of you that Mohammed Shami has put so much effort. I have not seen a fast bowler working so hard for domestic cricket games after playing so many international matches and taking many wickets in Tests, One-days and T20s,” he said.Shami has been one of India's most successful fast bowlers, especially on overseas tours. He picked up 145 wickets in 41 away Tests at an average of 30.33. At home, he was even more effective, taking 76 wickets at an average of 22.1.'You started with us in the red ball'Shukla also recalled Shami's early days in Bengal cricket and how he moved from the state's Under-23 team straight into the Ranji Trophy.The Bengal coach said he was the captain when Shami first joined the senior team and was happy to see how far the fast bowler had come.“I remember the day when you came to our Bengal nets for U23 games. You played Ranji Trophy directly from there. Our selectors were there and I was the captain at that time. You played from there and I was the captain that time and now the coach here,” he said.Shukla also spoke about Shami's strong connection with Bengal cricket and said his journey in red-ball cricket had come full circle.“You started with us in the red ball and now your Test match career ended with us. Our association is also very good. They have always supported you a lot. What you have done for Bengal is amazing. Mohammed Shami is and will always be a great inspiration. Love you, my brother. See you soon.”Shami to continue playing white-ball cricketAlthough Shami has retired from Tests, he will continue to play white-ball cricket.The fast bowler has been named in Bengal's 19-member squad for the Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy, which begins on November 14.Bengal will start its campaign against Karnataka at the Wankhede Stadium in Mumbai on November 14.Bengal are placed in Elite Group A along with Karnataka, Chandigarh, Jharkhand, Mizoram, Baroda, Uttar Pradesh and Rajasthan. All the league matches in the group will be played in Mumbai.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Josh Tongue out of England tour of Australia with toe injury as Jofra Archer and Adil Rashid impress in warm-up win over Western Australia
articles.summary: Jofra Archer takes 3-34 and Adil Rashid 4-35 as England bowl Western Australia out for 159 to clinch 92-run win in warm-up game in Perth; Harry Brook's side face Australia in the first of three ODIs on Friday, before five-match T20I series
articles.body:
The fast bowler sat out of England's 92-run warm-up win over Western Australia on Saturday and will return to the UK to undergo further assessment on the big toe on his left foot.

Jofra Archer and Adil Rashid made impressive returns to the fold as part of the victory in Perth. Archer, who was rested for the ODI tri-series in Pakistan, claimed 3-34 from his eight overs and Rashid, who was overlooked for most of that tour in favour of Liam Dawson, took 4-35 from 7.3 as WA were bowled out for 159, having been set 252 to win.

Ben Duckett continued his fine form with the bat, building on his back-to-back tri-series tons by top-scoring with 59 in an otherwise disappointing batting display by Harry Brook's side, having won the toss.

Brook (27) was a number of top-order batters to make starts but fail to convert to a big score, and the wicket of Sam Curran (12) in the 29th over had the tourists in a bit of a hole at 150-6.

Lower-order runs from Will Jacks (34) and Dawson (44no) helped lift England beyond 200 and to a competitive score, with the latter left stranded as they were ultimately bowled out for 251 in 48 overs - Brody Couch claimed 4-47 and Lance Morris 3-29.

In reply, Western Australia never looked likely to chase down England's target. Corey Wasley top-scored with 41, while Cameron Bancroft made 32 - a day after Usman Khawaja revealed that the entire Australian team knew about the ball-tampering scandal in Cape Town in 2018, for which Bancroft, Steve Smith and David Warner were punished.

Fit-again Jacob Bethell was not selected for England's warm-up match as he continues his return from the knee injury that has kept him sidelined since July.

England face Australia in the first of three ODIs on Friday, with five T20Is to follow.

articles.title: Bend it like Brar: Fiery Gurnoor heats up Wellington
articles.summary: WELLINGTON: Gurnoor Brar is a perfect recipe for a fast bowler.
articles.body: WELLINGTON: Gurnoor Brar is a perfect recipe for a fast bowler. The 26-year-old, who stands six-foot-five, has a repeatable action, and his ability to consistently hit that nagging hard length has rightly earned him the X-factor tag.However, the burly pacer has had his fair share of struggles in the ODI series against West Indies and England, where he leaked runs and conceded nearly 100 runs twice in his short career. Questions were raised about his lack of consistency, and it was clear that no matter how well-measured the ingredients were, the final dish needed the right stir -- which came as he arrived in New Zealand.For Gurnoor, New Zealand was the right opportunity to make his genetic gifts and hard work in the nets count, while silencing the critics who questioned the need for quicks over a wicket-taking spinner. India captain Shubman Gill has been vocal about preferring tall fast bowlers to make inroads during the middle-overs phase, and the skipper will be mighty pleased with how Gurnoor bent his back in both Auckland (3/44) and Wellington (4/30).The conditions were helpful for the pacers, but the ball still needed to be put in the right areas, and Brar did the job with aplomb. He wasn't carried away by the extra bounce, movement in the air or nip off the surface. Instead, he adjusted well to the "trampoline"-like uneven bounce and carry from the playing surface and ran through the opposition with some serious heat.Tom Latham, Glenn Phillips, Mitchell Santner and Nathan Smith were all undone by pace and extra bounce. The double-wicket burst in the 20th over was enough to put the home team on the mat, as Gurnoor continued relentlessly without compromising pace. This was exactly what Gill wanted during that phase: to prevent the opposition from forging a partnership. He finally got the results from the bowler he had long been working on and backed through tough times."My plan was simple - to hit my lengths and back my skills. Every day is a learning to get better, and ensure I adapt. I was looking to bowl full earlier and then use my bouncer at right moment," said Brar in the press conference later."Backing is very important for every player. There were flat tracks in India but we were backed there too by (the) management. They asked me to back my lengths and said khul ke ball daal (bowl freely). Shubman Gill backs everyone, doesn’t judge by performance. He himself has hunger for himself and the team," he added.The real test, however, will come on pitches that offer nothing for the bowlers. The debate between a fast bowler and a spinner will again take centre stage, but if there is enough spice in the surface, Gurnoor is ready to cook up a storm, and he has shown it in both matches so far.There is method behind the madness, and the subtle changes in release points and use of the width of the crease further make him unplayable on pitches like Wellington. Not to forget the occasional change in length he used to keep the batters guessing at the Hnry Stadium.Gurnoor has answered many questions. He will inject a lot of belief into the dressing room, and it is now up to the thinktank to figure out how to manage him in the build-up to the 2027 World Cup, where early-season pitches are expected to be better than the roads Gurnoor encountered at Lord's and Guwahati earlier this year.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: KL Rahul continues to underline his value to the Indian team with his ability to adapt to different match situations and deliver according to the demands
articles.body: KL Rahul continues to underline his value to the Indian team with his ability to adapt to different match situations and deliver according to the demands of the game. In the rain-hit second ODI against New Zealand in Wellington, while wickets kept tumbling at the other end, Rahul held his composure and remained unbeaten until the contest was decided by the Duckworth-Lewis-Stern (DLS) method, helping India secure a four-run victory.Rahul's calm approach and ability to negotiate challenging conditions earned him praise from former India all-rounder Irfan Pathan, who took to X to appreciate the wicketkeeper-batter's technique and temperament, particularly on difficult overseas pitches."KL Rahul has to be one of the most comfortable Indian batters on difficult overseas pitches. The technique, the composure and the calmness he brings to the crease are simply outstanding. A pleasure to watch him bat," Pathan wrote.Rahul stands tall amid India's batting collapseIndia's fast bowlers dominated the first innings, bowling New Zealand out for 134 in 41 overs. Auqib Nabi struck twice, including his maiden international wicket, while Gurnoor Brar removed Tom Latham and Glenn Phillips in a double-wicket maiden to leave the hosts reeling at 53/3.Daryl Mitchell top-scored with 55 off 104 balls, while Mitchell Santner contributed 31 as the pair added 59 runs for the sixth wicket. Brar finished with 4/30, while Nabi, Anshul Kamboj and Axar Patel picked up two wickets each.New Zealand fought back with the ball as Jacob Duffy dismissed Shubman Gill for a golden duck and Virat Kohli early in the chase. Kyle Jamieson further troubled India, reducing them to 47/4.Shreyas Iyer (30 off 46) and KL Rahul (26* off 38) attempted to rebuild the innings, but India slipped to 113/7 before rain interrupted play. With the visitors ahead on the DLS par score, India secured a four-run victory.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Josh Tongue ruled out of white-ball tour as Adil Rashid stars in warm-up
articles.summary: England fast bowler Josh Tongue is ruled out of the upcoming white-ball tour of Australia with a toe injury.
articles.body:
England fast bowler Josh Tongue has been ruled out of the upcoming white-ball tour of Australia with a toe injury.

The 28-year-old suffered the injury in Pakistan last month and didn't take part in the final two games of that tri-series.

He will now return to the UK for further assessment and miss the one-day and T20 matches in Australia, which start with an ODI in Perth on 13 November.

Tongue, who has taken 46 wickets in 17 matches this year, is likely to be back for the three-match Test series in South Africa in December, with the squad set to be named next week.

The white-ball tour of Australia will mark the first time England have played down under since the 2025-26 Ashes demolition.

Coach Brendon McCullum had previously said he wanted a strong team for the ODI leg of the trip to Australia in the build-up to the World Cup in southern Africa next year.

The New Zealander also conceded he would have to rotate his squad for the T20 leg, given England's schedule in a busy winter of five separate overseas tours.

Adil Rashid took four wickets as England beat Western Australia by 92 runs in their one-day warm-up match in Perth.

The 38-year-old was left out of the final three matches of the October tour of Pakistan and Sri Lanka but highlighted his importance down under, taking 4-35.

Fast bowler Jofra Archer chipped in with 3-34 as England ultimately cruised to victory.

It wasn't all straightforward though as a sloppy batting display saw England bowled out for 251.

Ben Duckett top scored with 49 while Liam Dawson was unbeaten for 44.

The hosts had England in trouble as they reached 60-1 before Rashid took a flurry of wickets, including Jayden Goodwin and Ashton Turner in successive deliveries.

Archer finished off the Western Australia tail, bowling them out for 159 and securing the win.

articles.title: ILT20 Season 5 introduces new batter zone Wide rule and two-way 60-second stop clock
articles.summary: The upcoming fifth season of the International League T20 will feature significant changes to its playing conditions, with a new \"batter zone\" to
articles.body: The upcoming fifth season of the International League T20 will feature significant changes to its playing conditions, with a new "batter zone" to determine Wide deliveries and the extension of the 60-second stop clock to the batting side.The revised regulations, which come into effect from the opening match on November 21, aim to ensure greater consistency in umpiring decisions and maintain a faster pace of play.The introduction of the batter zone marks one of the biggest changes. Under the new rule, a delivery will be called Wide if the entire ball passes outside the designated zone between the off-side and leg-side wide lines at the popping crease. A delivery passing above the standing batter’s head height will also be deemed a Wide.The rule will apply even if a batter moves across the crease to reach the delivery, provided no part of the ball passes within the designated zone and the batter makes no contact. An exception will apply to reverse sweeps and switch hits, for which the existing off-side Wide lines will be used.Another notable change concerns the 60-second stop clock, which will now apply to both batting and fielding teams. Previously enforced only on the fielding side, the regulation requires both batters to be ready for the next over within 60 seconds of the previous over ending.Teams will receive two warnings per innings. From the third offence onwards, the fielding side will be awarded five penalty runs. Certain situations, including injury treatment, strategic time-outs, weather interruptions and third-umpire reviews, will be exempt.The playing conditions also strengthen opportunities for regional cricketers. Each Playing XI must include at least two UAE players, two Afghanistan players and one player from an ICC Associate Member nation. This minimum combination must be maintained during substitutions and Super Sub changes, with specific provisions for concussion replacements.The fifth edition of the tournament will run from November 21 to December 20, 2026, featuring six franchises and several prominent international players.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates.
